title: SprintBound release cadence coordinator for synchronized runtime / console / API launches
creator: Maya Patel
description: Purpose: create a repeatable, sprint-bound release cadence ("SprintBound") that aligns runtime, console, and API launches to sprint boundaries with clear gating, communication templates, and rollback triggers. The goal is to reduce cross-team coordination friction, shorten lead time for coordinated feature launches, and ensure predictable capacity and blackout windows for customers and partners. Scope: product/pm coordination artifacts, cutover runbook, sprint gating checklist, capacity hedging calendar, and a shared calendar + Slack automation for notifications. Out of scope: full automation of deploy pipelines and infra provisioning (these remain with Eng).
acceptance_criteria: Shared SprintBound calendar published and subscribed by Runtime, Console, API, and Platform teams
Gating checklist completed and validated in two dry-run rehearsals with no critical blockers
Cutover runbook (owner list, rollback steps, monitoring signals, escalation path) approved by Eng and SRE
Automated Slack notification flow for pre-freeze, go/no-go, and rollback posted to #launch-ops
Capacity hedging slots published and reservation workflow defined for Dedicated customers
Two coordinated canary launches executed end-to-end across runtime + console + API with telemetry dashboards linked
updates: 2026-02-17: Kickoff meeting with Eng leads (runtime, infra, console) and Design. Agreed on SprintBound concept and sprint-aligned windows (every 2 sprints = major train; every sprint = micro train). Action: PM to draft gating checklist.

2026-02-23: Draft gating checklist circulated. Key gating signals: end-to-end latency within SLA, no untriaged critical alerts, rollout feature flags in place, and canary telemetry dashboards green. Feedback from SRE: add KV cache warmup verification and model-compat tests.

2026-03-02: Calendar prototype created (Google Calendar) with three lane types: Micro (sprint-level), Major (bi-sprint), Hotpatch (ad-hoc). Shared with stakeholders. Design to prepare communication template for pre-freeze and post-launch notes.

2026-03-04: Dependencies identified: ENG-41233 (runtime canary tooling), ENG-41987 (console rollout UI for flags), DES-2211 (communication banner and release banner designs). Eng estimates updated; ENG-41233 ETA 2026-03-18.

2026-03-08: Security and compliance flagged optional review for Private customers. Decided: only major trains touching private control plane require formal security signoff. Recording this as policy in the runbook.
2026-03-10: Approved cutover runbook draft posted to Drive. PM to schedule two rehearsals for 2026-03-22 and 2026-03-29. Next: coordinate with SRE for alert playbook integration.
next_steps: Book rehearsal 1 (2026-03-22): full dry-run with runtime canary, console flag rollout, and API gateway traffic routing; owners and observers assigned
Finalize gating checklist incorporating KV cache warmup and model-compat smoke tests
Create Slack automation for pre-freeze reminders (48h/8h/30m) and publish to #launch-ops
Confirm Dedicated capacity hedging reservation UI and communicate slots to sales/CS by 2026-03-18
risks: Runtime canary tooling (ENG-41233) slips, preventing full end-to-end rehearsal: mitigation = soft canary with synthetic traffic + manual verification
Capacity reservation conflicts for Dedicated customers during major trains: mitigation = reserve 20% buffer and publish blackout advisory
Cross-team misalignment on freeze windows (console vs runtime): mitigation = enforce sprint-bound windows and require calendar subscription from team leads
Unclear rollback ownership across service boundaries: mitigation = explicit owner roster in runbook and single escalation lead for each train
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2026-03-22): Dry-run 1 - internal rehearsal with simulated traffic, telemetry verification, and communications checklist
Phase 1 (2026-03-29): Dry-run 2 - quasi-production canary for low-risk feature set across EU region; test rollback and alerting paths
Phase 2 (2026-04-05): Pilot micro-train public release for runtime and API-only surface; monitor cost and latency signals for 72h
Phase 3 (2026-04-19): First synchronized major train (runtime + console + API) across two regions with customer-facing release notes and reserved Dedicated slots
Post-release: 7-day stability window with automated regression checks and retro scheduled in Cycle 2026-W16
